name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean anchors the race firmly Republican
Incumbent Mike Rogers holds a massive financial edge ($2.6M cash vs. under $10K for McInnis)
No competitive polling and no expert ratings flag the race as contested
Prediction markets price Rogers near certain to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Rogers: a deep-red R+23 district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of more than 250-to-1, with markets pricing his win at roughly 98 percent. With no polls or ratings suggesting any competitive threat, the forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-implied margin of about 20 points Republican.
model.watch: Any sign of meaningful Democratic fundraising or outside spending in the district would be the first signal the race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of R+23, and incumbent Mike Rogers is seeking another term after clearing his primary. His campaign has raised about $2.1 million and holds roughly $2.6 million on hand, while Democrat Lee McInnis has raised about $61,000 with under $10,000 available. No outside spending has been reported on either side.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert ratings for the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Rogers roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. The district's lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the absence of any competitive signals all point to a comfortable Republican hold in November.
